THIS MFA. CROB IS FILED UNDER ORDER XLI RULE 22 OF THE CPC READ WITH SECTION 173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLE ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 22.11.2017 PASSED IN MVC No.147/02014 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND PRINCIPAL JMFC, TARIKERE, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL ALONG WITH M.F.A.CROB, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The insurer has filed the appeal challenging the finding recorded by the Tribunal that the deceased while working as a cleaner of the lorry was killed and the insurer would thus be liable to pay compensation.
2. A cross-objection is also preferred by the claimants seeking for enhancement of compensation.
3. It is the contention of the insurer that the deceased was in no way related to the vehicle that it had insured.

It is contended that in the very claim petition in the column meant for intimating name and address of the employer, the same has been left blank and this indicates that the deceased was not employed by the owner of the lorry.
It is also contended that the complaint lodged by the police basically indicated that it was a case of hit and run and therefore, the lorry which it had insured cannot be held responsible.

It is also contended that the owner of the lorry to whom a notice had been served by the insurer had submitted a third party claim for in which he had stated that according to his driver the accident had not at all happened and was purely fabricated.
In the light of this, claimant petition ought not to have been allowed.

4. It is also contended that the evidence adduced before the Criminal Court where the driver of the lorry was prosecuted, it was stated by the witnesses that as on the date of the alleged incident only the driver and another cleaner was present and nobody else was travelling in the lorry.

It is,
therefore, submitted that the evidence when read in total would clearly indicate that the deceased has not died arising out of the motor vehicle accident i.e., out of the insured lorry.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants contended that it was admitted by the official of the Insurance Company itself that the deceased was working as a cleaner in the lorry and Smt Sudha vs V Kumara on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77242491/
4
in the light of this admission the entire edifice sought to be built up by the learned counsel for the insurer will have to be discarded.

He also stated that Ex.R-10, the deposition of cleaner which was sought to be relied upon by the insurer itself indicated that Girish, the cleaner categorically stated that on 05.07.2013 when he along with driver and the deceased were travelling in the lorry near M.C. Halli bus-stand, the deceased had fallen out of the lorry in a sleepy state.

He, therefore, stated that the admitted evidence on record itself indicated that the deceased was travelling in the lorry as a cleaner and therefore, the finding of the Tribunal was just and proper and is affirmed.
6. He also contended that the sums awarded as compensation were on the lower side, since the income taken was on the lower side and future prospects were not added.

7. As far as the question of involvement of the deceased with the insured lorry is concerned, it is to be stated here that at the very outset, the owner of the vehicle though entered appearance in person he did not take part in the proceedings and did not deny the assertions that the deceased was working as a cleaner.
Thus, the reliance sought to be made on the third party claim and the depositions rendered by the witnesses in the criminal case would really pale into the significance.

8. In the light of the clear admission of R.W.1, the official of the Insurance Company, which reads as follows- "zj jAi gdPig v 1 Jzgzg Qg v qg DV Pv wzg JAzg j"
9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is clear admission that the deceased was working as a cleaner in the lorry, the arguments that the deceased was in no way involved with the lorry will have to be discarded in its entirety.

10. It may also be pertinent to state here that even the third party claim that is sought to be relied on, the owner admits that the driver of his lorry met the deceased and both of them had dinner and thereafter the deceased went away.
It is the statement of the owner, which is relied upon by the insurer, which admits the fact that the driver of the lorry as well as the deceased were acquainted with one another.
It is to be stated here that the lorry in question was registered in Tamil Nadu and was travelling to Shimoga and returning back.

In such an event the probability of the driver meeting somebody at dinner and thereafter that person going away and subsequently it is found that the person who had dinner was killed creates a serious doubt as to the very statement given by the insurer.
The insurer sought to rely upon the evidence of Girish, who was examined as C.W.2 in the criminal case.
11. In the course of his cross-examination, Girish has stated as follows - "AP : 05-07-2013 gAz , Dg v v gdPiggg nJ 37 J 0502 jAi Zwz  JA   wg  tz  gdPig zAi vPr PU z."

Smt Sudha vs V Kumara on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77242491/
5 12.

In the light of this deposition, which is sought to be relied upon by the insurer, it cannot be in doubt at all that the deceased was travelling in the lorry and he fell out from the lorry while he was in a drowsy state.
13.

In my view, these factors when read in its entirety would clearly go to show that the deceased was travelling in the lorry and the fact that his body was found on the road, a presumption can be drawn that the death has occurred due to the motor vehicle accident.
The finding of the Tribunal on the basis of the admission of the insurer cannot be found fault with.

The argument of the learned counsel for the insurer that even if it is held that the deceased was a cleaner, the compensation payable can be only under the Workmen's Compensation Act cannot be accepted.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act give an option to a victim of the motor vehicle accident to choose either of the options i.e., either to seek compensation under the Employees'
Compensation Act or under the Motor Vehicles Act.
The fact that an option is given by itself is indicative of the fact that the law gives an opportunity to the victim to seek for compensation in the manner which is more beneficial to him.
Therefore, this argument cannot be accepted.
15. As far as compensation is concerned, in order to arrive at the loss of dependency, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.6,000/-.

As there is no credible evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State - 11 - Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2013, would be Rs.8,000/-.
16.
Since the deceased was aged 28 years and was self employed, 40% requires to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.11,200/-.

If 1/3rd is deducted towards personal expenses, his monthly income would be Rs.7,467/-.
17.

The income of the deceased for the purposes of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.7,467/-
18.
As the deceased was aged 28 years, a multiplier of '17' would have to be applied.

Consequently,
the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.15,23,268/- (Rs.7,467/- x 12 x '17') towards "loss of dependency".

19. The claimants being the wife and son, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/-
towards "loss of consortium" i.e., in all Rs.88,000/- and they would also - 12 - Smt Sudha vs V Kumara on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77242491/
6 be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the "conventional heads".

20. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 15,23,268/-

2 . Loss of Consortium 88,000/-
 3. Conventional Heads 33,000/-
 Total 16,44,268/-
21.

Thus, the claimant would be entitled for compensation of Rs.16,44,268/- as against Rs.11,56,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
22. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

On such deposit, Rs.7,50,000/- each is ordered to be invested in the name of claimants for a period of ten years in any Nationalised or Scheduled Bank of the choice of claimant - wife,
renewable for another three years, with liberty to withdraw the interest accrued thereon periodically.
After maturity, the Bank shall release the amount in favour of claimants without any further proceedings.
The remaining amount shall be released in favour of claimant - wife through account payee cheque after proper identification.
24. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
25. The appeal filed by insurer is dismissed and the cross-objection filed by claimants is accordingly allowed in part.

22. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
